newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady, seen easing slightly.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady, seen easing slightly.

text.p: Interbank rates were steady on Friday due to continued shortage of short-term funds, dealers said.
But maturities of Bank Negara bills next week could improve market liquidity and pull rates slightly lower, they said.
"There will be two maturities worth 1.5 billion ringgit next week and this should help ease the market a bit," said a dealer.
"If Bank Negara does not call for new issues, we should see rates coming off," he said.
One- and two-week money were traded at 9.0 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
The one-month rate was at 8.0/8.5 percent and three-month money was at 8.0/8.3 percent, both about unchanged from previous.
The overnight rate was expected to trade between 7.5 and 9.0 percent, dealers said.
The overnight fell to 7.5/8.0 percent on Thursday from 9.0 percent as foreign banks, flush with funds, offered lower.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down three points to 92.11, or an implied yield of 7.89 percent.
December contract was up two to 92.52, or 7.48 percent.
Futures dealers said the near month contracts were expected to face more selling pressure because of firm underlying interest rates.
